notes: PAYLOAD PROVENANCE — CORRECTED 11 SEP, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. When this baseline was recorded, the SDS text was added to the message BY HAND, because /api/chat built its content as 'File name: ' + fileName + '\n\nUser question: ' + userQuestion for any file that was not a PDF or an image — the document's contents never reached the model. The note here said this case was therefore IDEALISED rather than reproducible through the live path.

THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE. On 11 Sep the parsing was unified into lib/documentContent.ts and text/plain was added as a branch it had never had, so /api/chat now reads a .txt and sends its contents. **This case is reproducible through the live path**: uploading isopropyl-alcohol-sds.txt to /compliance and asking the same question now sends the same document to the same model. The recorded `actual` predates that change and was produced by the hand-built payload — so it is a valid baseline for the content, and a re-run is what would confirm the live path matches it.

Composition differs in one respect worth knowing before comparing a re-run: the live path puts the document blocks first and 'File name: … User question: …' after them, whereas this recorded run had the filename, then the document, then the question, in a single text block. Same information, different order.

CITATION CONFIDENCE IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS THE SEVEN EXPECTED FACTS. Two were retrieved from the live eCFR API in this session and are quoted from that response: 49 CFR 173.202 (UN-spec packaging) and 49 CFR 172.704 (hazmat employee training). The other FIVE were NOT checked against any source — labeling/marking (cited by the model as 172.400 and 172.301), shipping papers with emergency contact (172.200 and 172.604), carrier acceptance (177.817), and the three facts stated in the input document itself (UN1219, Hazard Class 3, Packing Group II). An empty citation and a populated one DO NOT carry the same confidence, and the section numbers for the unchecked four come from the model's own answer, which is the thing under test — they are not independent corroboration.

Retrieval was via the eCFR API because the human-facing eCFR URL redirects to a bot-block interstitial (302 to unblock.federalregister.gov). The citation_url recorded on each fact is the human-readable one, which is what a person should follow; it is not the URL that was fetched. Also note the fetch is model-mediated — the page was read back by a summarising model, not transcribed by hand — so 'primary-source-retrieved' is the honest ceiling here, not 'verified'.

The response came back wrapped in ```json fences despite the system prompt's 'No other text. No markdown. No backticks.' askAI returns raw text; only askAIJson strips fences, and /api/chat calls askAI.

system_prompt_sha256 is recorded so that 'the prompt changed' is detectable. TODO 2.8 says re-run after every prompt change or model upgrade — this is what makes that checkable rather than remembered.
